column1: # ---------------- THE SERVICE MOVED AGAIN, AND THIS TIME IT CHANGED ITS NAME ----------------
*** THE OLD ADDRESS IS STILL DEAD AND THE SERVICE IS ALIVE SOMEWHERE ELSE ***
column2: re-probed 11 October: www.national.archsrch.gov.za/sm300cv/smws/sm300dl still answers 503 over http and times out over https, exactly as on 27 September; nationalarchives.gov.za/naairs.htm is still 404. THE MAIN SITE NOW CARRIES A LINK TO /search/ AND THAT IS THE WHOLE SERVICE.

column1: *** https://www.nationalarchives.gov.za/search/ — "NATIONAL ARCHIVAL INFORMATION SEARCH SYSTEM" ***
column2: page title NarsaSearchPortal, subtitle "National Automated Archival Information Retrieval System" — the same words NAAIRS stands for. It is an Angular application, free, no account, and it answers 200.

column1: AND IT IS THE FULL HOLDING, TWENTY REPOSITORIES
column2: ECKAR King William's Town · GEN the Genealogical Society's gravestone data · HER the Bureau of Heraldry · KAB Cape Town · LAR Limpopo · MAN the national registers of manuscripts and photographs · NAB Pietermaritzburg · NAR National Archives Repository · NCAR Northern Cape · NFVSA film, video and sound · NWAR North-West · OVM audio-visual · ROS oral sources · RSA ALL REPOSITORIES AT ONCE · SAB central government since 1910 · TAB the former Transvaal · TBD Durban · TBE Port Elizabeth · TBK Cape Town Records Centre · VAB Free State.

column1: how to query it, for whoever comes next
column2: the UI is a four-keyword form with Contains/AND/OR and a year range. Underneath it POSTs to /search-api/api/search with {"repositoryCode":"RSA","keywords":[{"keyword":"X","operator":"AND","matchType":"CONTAINS","enabled":true}],"hasDigitalObject":false,"startComparand":"GE","endComparand":"LE","chronologicalOrder":"ASC","sortBy":"RELEVANCE","page":0,"limit":2000} and returns JSON with `total`, `results[]` and facets. THE ROUTE /search/search?repository=RSA 404s IF TYPED DIRECTLY — there is no server-side fallback for the app's routes, so the portal must be entered at /search/ and the repository clicked.

column1: and one caveat worth having before anybody trusts a count
column2: A MULTI-WORD KEYWORD IS NOT A PHRASE. "LEIBHOLZ GERTRUD" returns 559 records, which is more than either word alone would suggest and nothing like a phrase match. One surname per keyword box.

column1: # ---------------- AND IT IS THE COMPLETE DATABASE, WHICH SETTLES THE 27 SEPTEMBER BOUND ----------------
*** NARSSA STILL PUBLISHES THE TWO-DATABASE WARNING, AND IT NAMES THIS PORTAL AS THE COMPLETE ONE ***
column2: the notice on www.nationalarchives.gov.za/search-collections is unchanged and still live: “NARSSA is in the process of migrating more than 8.3 MILLION ENTRIES from the old NAAIRS database to the new database and therefore ‘fulltext search’ (new database) WILL NOT DISPLAY ALL THE RECORDS IN THE SYSTEM. In the meantime NARSSA makes both databases available for use by the public. Using the ‘Search Old NAAIRS database’ will provide a more complete search…” *** AND THEN: “TO SEARCH THE COMPLETE DATABASE PLEASE CLICK ON: Search NAAIRS Database →” — AND THE HREF ON THAT LINK IS https://www.nationalarchives.gov.za/search/, WHICH IS THE PORTAL USED HERE. ***

column1: why that matters more than the find
column2: negative #18 carried a bound added on 27 September which said that the archive could not establish WHICH of the two databases had answered its searches, and that “the balance of evidence is that the old complete database answered” — evidence, not proof. FOR TODAY'S SEARCHES IT IS NOW PROOF, FROM THE ARCHIVE'S OWN PAGE: this is the database NARSSA itself calls complete. The uncertainty is not argued away, it is replaced.

column1: and the “two databases” are not two addresses any more
column2: the old Search Manager endpoint is dead, the fulltext search is a separate and admittedly partial thing, and the complete holding is now served by one Angular portal with a repository selector. A reader of the 27 September bound would have gone looking for “Search Old NAAIRS database” as a distinct link. IT IS THIS ONE.

column1: # ---------------- THE CONTROL, FIRST, BECAUSE THE WHOLE POINT IS A NEGATIVE ----------------
*** SMITH 47,936 · SCHMIDT 3,418 ***
column2: the instrument is alive and it is large. Every zero below is a zero from a working search.

column1: # ---------------- NEGATIVE #18 IS RE-RUN UNDER SIX SPELLINGS AND IT HOLDS ----------------
*** LEIBHOLZ 0 · LEIPHOLZ 0 · LEIBHOLTZ 0 · LEIPHOLTZ 0 · LAIBHOLZ 0 · LEIBHOLS 0 ***
column2: No Leibholz appears anywhere in the South African archives was searched under LEIBHOLZ ALONE and row 247 called it "the exact shape of the 1975 error" — the volume that had been read and called empty until the pattern was widened to Le[iy][bp]h. IT IS NOW WIDENED HERE AND IT SURVIVES. The eighth spelling, LEIPHOLZ, which the Berliner Adressbuch prints as its own cross-reference and which has produced four people in the Berlin registers this month, HAS NOW BEEN PUT TO A SOUTH AFRICAN ARCHIVE AND RETURNS NOTHING.

column1: the one near miss, recorded so it is not mistaken for one
column2: LEIBHOLD returns 1. A different surname, and not a spelling this family is written under anywhere.

column1: # ---------------- NEGATIVES #9 AND #10 ARE RE-RUN AND THEY HOLD TOO ----------------
*** LUWINSKI 7 · LUWINSKY 1 · LEWINSKI 5 · LOWINSKY 7 — AND NO NATURALISATION AND NO IMMIGRATION FILE UNDER ANY OF THEM ***
column2: row 247's note said #9 and #10 were searched under LUWINSKI alone "and this archive knows the South African record writes him LUWINSKY in a 1948 court file". LUWINSKY RETURNS EXACTLY THAT ONE FILE AND NOTHING ELSE — TAB WLD 1950/1948, the divorce, which the archive has had since September. The widening adds no naturalisation and no immigration paper. LUWINSKA, LOWINSKI, LOWINSKA, LUWINSKIE, LUVINSKI, LOWINSKE and LUWINS all return zero.

column1: and LEWINSKI's five and LOWINSKY's seven are the two strands already ruled out
column2: LOWINSKY's seven are Mark/Marcus William Lowinsky of the 1880s and 1890s Transvaal, the Simonstown pottery lease, and Rupert Esmond Lowinsky's 1955 Cape estate — the Johannesburg strand this archive excluded on a date, in print eleven years before Kurt landed. LEWINSKI's five are the Erwin/Bella/Meinhard family already excluded on 16 September. NOTHING HERE REOPENS EITHER.

column1: # ---------------- AND THE SWEEP FOUND TWO COURT FILES THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT HAVE ----------------
*** ZA TAB WLD_0_1878/1956_1 — "ILLIQUID CASE. RESTITUTION OF CONJUGAL RIGHTS. KURT LUWINSKI VERSUS FRANCES (FORMERLY SEFTON, FORMERLY BERNER, BORN HOSTOWSKY)." ***
column2: A SEVENTH CASE, and site/src/data/litigation.json holds six. KURT MARRIED FRANCES HOSTOWSKY ON 29 FEBRUARY 1956 — the archive has that from the South African civil marriage index, with her age given as 43 — AND SUED HER FOR RESTITUTION OF CONJUGAL RIGHTS IN THE SAME YEAR. In South African practice a restitution order is the first step of a divorce. THE MARRIAGE LASTED MONTHS.

column1: *** ZA TAB WLD_0_126/1959_1 — "ILLIQUID CASE. JUDICIAL SEPARATION. FRANCES EISENHARDT (BORN HOSTOWSKI) VERSUS ROLF." ***
column2: she married ROLF EISENHARDT ON 23 MAY 1958, which this archive has had for days, AND SUED HIM FOR JUDICIAL SEPARATION WITHIN THE YEAR. Not Kurt's business and not kin to anyone here; recorded because it completes a person the archive half-held and because it was found in the same two queries.

column1: and the archival reference for the 1958 marriage, which the archive had only from an index
column2: ZA KAB HAWC_1/3/58/1/53_183_1, "MARRIAGE REGISTER. CAPE TOWN AND WYNBERG. ROLF EISENHARDT AND FRANCES LUWINSKI (FORMERLY SEFTON, FORMERLY BERNER, BORN HOSTOWSKI)." A register volume with a shelf mark, not a search result.

column1: # ---------------- THREE FAMILY SURNAMES PUT TO A SOUTH AFRICAN ARCHIVE FOR THE FIRST TIME ----------------
KERGER 3 — and two of the three are IMMIGRATION PAPERS
column2: ZA KAB PIO_545_24017E_1 "IMMIGRATION PAPERS. A KERGER AND FAMILY." · ZA KAB PIO_1591_70027E_1 "IMMIGRATION PAPERS. L KERGER." · ZA NAB SGO_III/1/121_SG3534/1897_1 "H KERGER TO SURVEYOR-GENERAL RE LAND AT POLELA." AGNES LEIBHOLZ WAS BORN KERGER, 10 MARCH 1889, and died in Berlin's orbit; NOTHING CONNECTS HER TO ANY OF THESE and Kerger is an ordinary German surname. Recorded because the surname had never been tried here and because an initial and "and family" is what an unindexed immigration file looks like.

column1: SCHMUL 5 and POLLNOW 1, both long shots and both now closed
column2: Schmul: a Netherlands vice-consul in Johannesburg, a Dorothea Meyer born Schmul (TAB MHG 4267/57), a committal at East London, a Mirsky immigration file where Schmul is a FORENAME, and a 1922 Free State criminal case. Pollnow: one 1955 opposed application, Hilde Pollnow born Silbermann. FRIEDERICA SCHMUL AND WILHELMINE POLLNOW ARE SALLY LEIBHOLZ'S WIFE AND MOTHER AND NEITHER OF THEM CAME TO AFRICA. These are recorded as tried and empty, not as leads.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT THIS CLOSES AND WHAT IT OPENS ----------------
*** ROW 247'S RE-RUNNING HALF IS NO LONGER BLOCKED AND IS NOW DONE FOR THE THREE THAT MATTERED ***
column2: #18, #9 and #10 were the three the row named. All three are re-run under every spelling this archive writes the names in, against a live control, and ALL THREE SURVIVE AS PUBLISHED. They should be reclassified from PROVISIONAL to WIDE.

column1: and five work list rows lose their blocker
column2: every row owned by "the National Archives of South Africa — NAAIRS is down" can now be worked. The service did not come back at the address this archive was watching; IT CAME BACK SOMEWHERE ELSE UNDER A DIFFERENT NAME, which is the second time in a month that a dead URL has been mistaken for a dead service — the first was negative #21, withdrawn on exactly that ground.

column1: no bot gate was worked around
column2: the portal is open, needs no account, and its own user interface issues the same POST this file used. The requests were made from the portal's own page, one surname at a time, and nothing was scraped in bulk.
